title: GRE tunnels to ZIA: requirements, bandwidth and deployment

prose.text: GRE is the tunnel for sites whose router can build it. This subject covers what the tunnel needs and how it scales; health checks and failover are in [[zia.traffic-forwarding.gre-failover]], and which method to pick is in [[zia.traffic-forwarding.methods]].

Where to build it.

checks.do: Whether the tunnel's source IP is a provisioned static IP.
Whether the inner addresses are NATed, which sets the tunnel to 1 Gbps or 250 Mbps.
Whether the primary and secondary VIPs are in different data centers.

overview.statement: A GRE tunnel functions like a VPN without encryption: a GRE-capable router encapsulates the packet and sends it across the public network to the Zscaler service. GRE adds a 4-byte header.

quotes: A GRE tunnel functions like a VPN but without encryption; it transports packets from one endpoint to another through the public network.
A Generic Routing Encapsulation (GRE) tunnel is ideal for forwarding internet-bound traffic from your corporate network to the Zscaler service.
A GRE-capable router encapsulates a payload packet inside a GRE packet.
GRE = 4 bytes header

static-ip-required.statement: The tunnel's egress port needs a static IP address: the perimeter router must support GRE and its egress port must have a static IP.

quotes: Your organization’s perimeter edge router must support GRE and its egress port must have a static IP address.
If your corporate router supports GRE and its egress port has a static IP address, Zscaler recommends that you configure a GRE tunnel

source-ip-provisioned.statement: A tunnel's source IP must already be provisioned as a static IP in the service, and the static IP list can be filtered to addresses not yet used by a tunnel.

expect.description: The source IP address of the GRE tunnel. This is typically a static IP address in the organization or SD-WAN. This IP address must be provisioned within the Zscaler service using the /staticIP endpoint.
Set to true to get only the static IP addresses that are not yet associated to a GRE tunnel.

bandwidth-limit.statement: Zscaler supports at most 1 Gbps per GRE tunnel when the internal endpoint addresses are not NATed and 250 Mbps when they are (source NAT, including source PAT).

quotes: Zscaler supports a maximum bandwidth of 1 Gbps for each GRE tunnel if the internal tunnel endpoint IP addresses are not source network address translated (NATed). If the internal tunnel endpoint IP addresses are source NATed, then Zscaler can only support up to 250 Mbps of traffic for each tunnel.
The restriction also applies when performing source NAT with source PAT.

nat-limit-reason.statement: The NAT limit exists because the service load-balances GRE traffic over multiple servers by the internal IP addresses of the tunnel; when every packet carries the same internal source address the balancer cannot spread it across nodes.

quotes: If the internal tunnel endpoint IP addresses are source NATed, then Zscaler can only support up to 250 Mbps of traffic for each tunnel.
This is because the Zscaler service uses the internal IP addresses of the GRE tunnel to load-balance GRE traffic over multiple servers.
If the internal source IP address is the same for all traffic across multiple GRE tunnels, then the load-balancer cannot be effective in balancing the traffic across different nodes

scale-out.statement: Above 1 Gbps, Zscaler recommends more tunnels with different public source IP addresses, each with a backup: 2 Gbps is two primary and two backup tunnels, 3 Gbps is three and three.

quotes: If your organization wants to forward more than 1 Gbps of traffic, Zscaler recommends configuring more GRE tunnels with different public source IP addresses.

For example, if your organization forwards 2 Gbps of traffic, you can configure two primary GRE tunnels and two backup GRE tunnels. If your organization forwards 3 Gbps of traffic, you can configure three primary GRE tunnels and three backup GRE tunnels.

client-persistence.statement: With several egress IPs, client persistence should be maintained (load balancer, ECMP or other), because a server that checks persistence refuses connections arriving from a different egress IP.

quotes: When configuring multiple GRE tunnels, you should maintain client persistence to avoid issues because a server with persistence checking refuses connection to different egress IP addresses.
You can use a Load Balancer (LB), ECMP, or other means to maintain persistence.

internal-router.statement: Zscaler's recommended deployment is two tunnels from an internal router behind the firewall, a primary to a Public Service Edge in one data center and a secondary to another. The tunnel source is a public IP configured on the router's loopback interface, the firewall needs a rule allowing GRE from the router, and internal IP addresses stay visible for policy and logging.

quotes: Zscaler recommends that you configure two GRE tunnels from an internal router behind the firewall to the Public Service Edge for Internet & SaaS (ZIA): a primary tunnel from the router to a Public Service Edge in one data center and a secondary tunnel from the router to a Public Service Edge in another data center.
the GRE tunnel source IP address is a public IP address that is configured on the loopback interface of the router
On the firewall, you'll need to define a rule that allows GRE traffic from the router.
This type of deployment provides visibility into the internal IP addresses, which can be used for the Zscaler security policies and logging.

border-router.statement: If an internal router is not feasible, a tunnel can be built from the border router, which must send internet-bound traffic to the Public Service Edges and requires NAT disabled on the firewall so internal IPs remain visible.

quotes: If configuring GRE tunnels from an internal router to the Public Service Edges is not feasible, then you can configure a GRE tunnel from your border router to the Public Service Edge.
You also need to disable NAT on your firewall to provide internal IP address visibility to the Public Service Edges.
In this type of deployment, you need to configure the border router to send internet-bound traffic to the Public Service Edges.

explicit-via-global-edges.statement: For explicit proxy mode over GRE in an environment with no default route, the tunnel is used with the Global Public Service Edge addresses 185.46.212.88 to .93, .97 and .98. These are dummy addresses that no Public Service Edge listens on but all know about, so traffic is routed to them through a GRE or IPSec tunnel and a PAC file directs users there.

quotes: To configure GRE tunnels with the explicit proxy mode in no default route environment, use the following set of global Public Service Edge IP addresses:
The addresses of these Public Service Edges do not listen for traffic but are dummy addresses that all Public Service Edges know about.
Ensure that you route the traffic destined to the Global Public Service Edge IP address through a GRE or an IPSec tunnel.
Use PAC files to direct the corporate user traffic to the Global Public Service Edge IP address.

primary-backup-per-egress.statement: Zscaler requires primary and backup tunnels from every internet egress location and, where applicable, from each internet service provider.

quotes: Zscaler requires building primary and backup GRE tunnels from every internet egress location and, if applicable, from each internet service provider.

provisioning.statement: A tunnel is provisioned either through a Zscaler Support ticket or by self-provisioning in the Admin Console; regional surcharge and premium data centers are excluded from the data center picker because of possible extra cost or specialized usage restrictions.

quotes: Submit a Zscaler Support ticket or contact Zscaler Support to receive the GRE tunneling configuration.
Self-provision a GRE tunnel using the Zscaler Admin Console
regional surcharge and premium data centers are excluded from the picker due to possible additional costs or specialized usage restrictions

vip-selection.statement: A tunnel names a primary and a secondary destination VIP; when neither is given the SDK picks the closest recommended VIPs. The within-country flag restricts VIPs to the source IP's country, and the unnumbered flag supports automated SD-WAN provisioning with no internal tunnel addresses.

quotes: Note: If the `primary_dest_vip` and `secondary_dest_vip` aren't specified then the closest recommended VIPs will be automatically chosen.

expect.description: Restrict the data center virtual IP addresses (VIPs) only to those within the same country as the source IP address
This is required to support the automated SD-WAN provisioning of GRE tunnels, when set to true gre_tun_ip and gre_tun_id are set to null
The primary destination data center and virtual IP address (VIP) of the GRE tunnel
The secondary destination data center and virtual IP address (VIP) of the GRE tunnel

mtu-mss.statement: MTU and MSS for the tunnel are calculated from the WAN interface: for a 1,500-byte WAN, GRE MTU is 1,500 - 20 - 4 = 1,476 and GRE MSS is 1,476 - 20 - 20 = 1,436. An incorrect MTU causes fragmentation and degraded performance.

quotes: Zscaler recommends that you calculate the maximum transmission unit (MTU) and maximum segment size (MSS) values on the GRE tunnel based on the MTU and MSS configuration of the WAN interface. An incorrectly configured MTU results in higher fragmentation, leading to performance degradation.
GRE MSS = GRE MTU (1,476) – IP (20) – TCP (20) = 1,436

api-surface.statement: Tunnels are managed at /greTunnels; recommended destination VIPs come from /vips/recommendedList (also grouped by data center at /vips/groupByDatacenter), and /orgProvisioning/ipGreTunnelInfo returns IP addresses with their tunnel details.

expect.description: Gets a list of recommended GRE tunnel virtual IP addresses (VIPs), based on source IP address or latitude/longitude coordinates.
Gets a list of IP addresses with GRE tunnel details.
Gets a list of recommended GRE tunnel virtual IP addresses (VIPs), grouped by data center, based on source IP address or latitude/longitude coordinates.
Gets all provisioned GRE tunnel information.

mss-symptom.title: Symptom of an unclamped GRE MSS
mss-symptom.detail: Unverified legacy statement: Failing to clamp MSS is a common cause of browsing works but large file transfers hang complaints under GRE. No captured source states it; operator experience or a tenant observation would settle it.

ipv6-coverage.title: IPv6 coverage of GRE tunnels
ipv6-coverage.detail: Unverified legacy statement: GRE and IPSec tunnel configuration may not cover IPv6 traffic; check router and firewall capability explicitly. No captured source states it; a lab test would settle it.

premium-dc-support.title: Whether premium data centers can be used with a Support ticket
premium-dc-support.detail: Unverified legacy statement: Premium/surcharge data centers are excluded from the VIP picker UI and require a Support ticket. No captured source states it; Zscaler Support or a vendor article would settle it.
